module.name: Serewater March — Censer Hill
module.description: Installed situations share this persistent world.

entities.name: Ash the cave hound, cave scavenger
A concealed stair joins the name room and family crypt
The waxed refuge register survives. Its family numbers identify the remains in the crypt; the flood refuge belonged to three settlements, not the salvage company.
The hoist counterweight releases when the cable takes weight. Delving can pin it; a survey line can brace it. Otherwise the leading companion takes the risk.
The split preservative crock vents poison when its floorboard tilts. Delving can pin the board; a line braces it. An antidote removes poison after exposure.
The bronze shutter strikes and weakens an unready intruder. The release can be pinned or braced. The court itself is safe to converse in.
A chalk fault connects the founders gallery to the exposed drainage entrance. Once learned, this return route remains usable.
Pell surveyed the dry stair: vestibule, workshop, stores, refuge stair, then the great hall. The hoist is not the only descent.
The company license covers the tram bearing and foundry machinery. It does not cover registered burials. Edda leaves for Reedwake if her permit expires.
The Mortuary Custodian admits a company bearing Iven’s custody writ and knowledge of the surviving register. It can also be bypassed by the line descent from the family crypt.

actions.name: Ask Nera how to prepare
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Plan your return before your descent,' says Nera. 'The inn costs one shared ration for six hours. I sell finite medicines and rations. The dry stores hold a line; take it before trying the hoist or deep clefts. Antidote treats poison, not a crushed skull. Your purchases belong to the companion you name.'
actions.speaker: march__nera

actions.name: Ask why the town cares about Censer Hill
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Bronze buys work; washed-out bones buy grief. Edda needs the tram bearing. Iven needs names kept with their dead. Pell has not come home. You can choose one of those reasons, or none. Bring back a useful tool and the next expedition may reach somewhere the first could not.'
actions.speaker: march__nera

actions.name: Ask Iven about the Custodian and burial custody
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'I do not command a monster by feeling righteous,' Iven says. 'Its mandate is written. Bring word that the name register survives. A company trained in burial lore, or recognized under the Free Fellowship compact, can carry my custody writ. The guardian honors a named record and that writ. Killing it will open the way too, but leaves no keeper below.'
actions.speaker: march__iven

actions.name: Show Iven the surviving name record and request custody
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: Iven compares your account to his damaged name slips. 'I was wrong to think it lost. Carry my custody writ. This permits supervised access, not ownership of every burial. The record gives the people back their names.'
actions.speaker: march__iven

actions.name: Ask Edda what she is salvaging
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'A bronze bearing, not someone's grandmother,' Edda says. 'It is in the hoist room. Bring the actual bearing to me and I pay six coins from my own purse. I can wait only until watch {march__expiresAt(march__permit)}. I will go home rather than risk my crew underground. The upper stores connect to a dry stair; you do not owe the hoist your neck.'
actions.speaker: march__edda

actions.name: Ask Pell what happened
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'The rack fell when they hauled the bearing,' Pell says. 'Shift it and get me back to the quay. The stores have a line and a dry stair. I will not carry Edda's bronze just because I know the way.'
actions.speaker: march__pell

actions.name: Ask Pell where to go now
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Home, through the vestibule and yard,' Pell says. 'Use Escort if you want me with you. I do not follow people who walk away without me. If you go deeper, I will wait here.'
actions.speaker: march__pell

actions.name: Speak with Pell after returning
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: Pell presses a sketch into the journal. 'You brought me out. The chalk fault from the founders gallery reaches the drain; look for scratches underground. Take the time to choose a technique at the inn before you go back.'
actions.speaker: march__pell

actions.name: Address the Mortuary Custodian
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: Bronze fingers fold. 'CUSTODY IS NOT CONQUEST. NAME THE DEAD. BEAR THE KEEPER’S WRIT. OR RETURN BY THE WAY YOU CAME.' Its mandate recognizes those specific records. The same words are cut into its bronze breastplate.
actions.speaker: march__custodian

observations.text: Barges nose into reed-fringed piles. Wool bales and repaired hulls keep Reedwake working. Censer Hill rises beyond the willow causeway: a derelict foundry above old flood-refuge chambers. West are Nera's supplies and the inn; east, the common shrine and salvage office. Washed-out burial bones trouble the boatmen. No one agrees that everything beneath the hill is salvage.

Dry boots hang above the hearth. A shared ration buys six hours on the upstairs pallets, with full recovery for living companions and treatment of bleeding. Poison requires an antidote or purification. The dead remain dead. A chalk board lists the road to Censer Hill and a note: 'Bring a line. Leave enough strength to come back.'

Two small altars face one another: the Keeper of Names, whose dead must not be lost, and the Returning Current, patron of safe journeys and reciprocal aid. Iven sorts water-stained name slips. His institution, not an anonymous force of magic, claims custody of Censer Hill's named burials.

Oilcloth, line, salves and carefully counted rations fill the shelves. Nera equips repeat customers; she cannot restock a limitless expedition. Physical medicines here are unique bottles. Choose their recipient when buying, then use or equip them from the party inventory. The climbing line in the hill's dry stores may open routes that strength alone cannot.

The licensed company's ledger is open to a sketch of a bronze tram bearing. Edda has gone to the upper workshop; a permit deadline may bring her back empty-handed. The office is not the burial society. A metal claim does not convey ownership of human remains.

Willow roots bind the old stone causeway across the reed floodplain. Waterfowl lift from the sedges. The dry ridge climbs to the foundry yard; a low path leads to the exposed drain. A rooted boar bars the drain path, but a woodcraft company can read its warning posture and pass without violence. A bed of edible marsh cress grows beside the willow poles; woodcraft can gather finite rations. The river mark rises later today; the ridge remains dry.

Short grass and hawthorn cling to pale limestone. Sheep bells sound from distant Chalkcross. A hazel stand offers finite edible nuts to a woodcraft company. The foundry yard lies uphill, Reedwake below. A worn hillside track descends toward the drain: a second way into the hill, not a portal to its end.

Rusting tram rails cross an ash-grown yard. The roofless vestibule enters level I; the causeway and ridge return to town. A surveyor's scratches mark a possible climb between this yard and the hoist shaft. Without a proper line the shaft is too exposed. The foundry once served all three river settlements; no faction built it alone.

A broken culvert breathes cold air beside the reeds. At low water it reaches level II's sluice walk. A chalk passage also returns here once its route is learned underground. The tide board's red notch means the culvert is under water; this blocks the entrance, not every way out.

A broken rack pins Pell's coat and boot beneath a timber. He is alive, angry and reachable. You can shift the rack and escort him back through ordinary routes. The workshop lies beyond. A survey board names the dry stores and an upper hoist; helping Pell need not mean carrying out Edda's salvage contract.

Half-cast bells lean against the wall. Edda's chalk circles identify reusable bronze, while burial marks below the stair declare another institution's custody. Routes reach the vestibule, casting gallery and dry stores. You can find wealth here without descending to the dead.

Ceramic moulds make narrow islands beneath a collapsed roof. A cave hound scavenges at the hoist entrance. You can fight, use ranger woodcraft to leave it unprovoked, or return through the stores to the dry refuge stair. Its survival does not reset when you leave.

A cracked furnace opens beneath the gallery. Slag-glass catches the light; a narrow workers’ loop joins the workshop and gallery. The safe floor here allows you to pause, count supplies and decide between the dry stores and the exposed hoist. The cold hearth holds only weathered slag; the great bell mould has split.

A slack cable loops around the hoist drum. The uncovered counterweight hangs above a narrow descent to the upper landing. A scored timber records how it releases. Read it before committing a leading companion. A line can brace the mechanism; a delving specialist can disarm it. The climbing scar rises to the yard.

A collapsed oilcloth chest stands against the inner wall. The dry stair descends to the refuge without touching the hoist counterweight. Taking the line gives a real tool to a particular companion; it is not a flag that ends the adventure.
Soot-black stone steps descend from the stores. Refuge arrows point toward the flood hall; return arrows point up. Even when the drain floods, this stair remains a dependable exit.
The hoist cage has sunk into gravel. A narrow crawl joins the flood hall; above is the spent or still-dangerous counterweight crossing. Returning by the dry stair avoids trusting the mechanism twice.

Three settlements carved their household tallies on the refuge pillars. The flood hall connects the dry stair, hoist landing, old kitchens and sluice walk. This was a shelter before it became an ossuary. The voices of the dead are not a substitute for the surviving register.

A sealed preservative crock has split beneath the route to the name room. Greenish dust traces the floor. The warning label identifies the vapour and the release; you can prepare an antidote, disarm it with delving, brace its lid with a line, risk exposure, or reach the lower vaults another way.

Waxed shelves and a funeral lampstand occupy the dry wall. The register identifies the families in the crypt; it is evidence of people, not proof that all valuables are yours. Tiny shining lettering on the rear wall suggests a concealed stair. An equipped names lantern makes that lettering legible.

Stone gutters run from the exposed drain through the old refuge. A dry wall-walk reaches the lower landing even when the entrance culvert floods. Flood marks record the next rise; the refuge stair remains an alternative way home.
A stair of river-smoothed limestone leaves the sluice walk and turns toward the family crypt. The path back is visible. Cold incense lies in the air. Old footmarks turn toward the family crypt.

Small alcoves hold bundled remains under numbered tiles. The hidden stair from the name room emerges behind a screen here. The Custodian's court stands ahead. A cleft leads to the founders' gallery, but descending it safely requires a line: lawful passage and physical bypass are different advantages.

A bronze dais rises beneath articulated burial shutters. It is funerary bronze and stone, bound to recognize a custody writ supported by the surviving names. It does not read your conscience. Present lawful records, fight it, or turn back. The shutter route offers another dangerous path toward the founders' gallery; its scratched warning is readable before crossing.

Named stone drawers remain in order. An offering tray stands before the named drawers. The guardian's permission admits you; it has not sold the dead. The court remains behind you. If you killed the guardian, its heavy footsteps have fallen silent.

Three bronze founders hold tools rather than crowns. Their plinths name the flood-refuge compact of Reedwake, Chalkcross and Brackenholt. A chalk passage leads toward the surface. A line can also climb to the family crypt. A small purse and a funerary technique remain; choosing a reward does not end the campaign.

A pale fault runs upward to the exposed drain. Survey scratches on this side reveal the way through, permanently adding it to your usable geography. Once known, it becomes another route for retreat or a second expedition. Your old footprints remain undisturbed beneath the dust.
The red notch is under water. The culvert entrance is closed to you; an occupied sluice walk can still leave. The ridge, dry stair and learned chalk route remain available.
Edda has withdrawn from the hill. Her permit deadline elapsed whether you were there or not. The bearing remains where this history left it.
Pell is back at the river, alive because someone actually escorted him out. His old place in the vestibule is empty.
The Custodian lies still. Its burial chain hangs severed from a bronze hand. This is a lasting opening, and a lasting loss of the burial society’s protection.
The Custodian steps aside under the written mandate. Its force and the named burials remain intact.
The lifted rack rests against the wall. Pell is free and waiting. The workshop lies ahead; the yard leads home. Escort moves the company and Pell together along an ordinary route.
The lifted timber rack has been left against the wall. Pell has departed. His old survey scratches still point toward the workshop and dry stores.
The cave hound lies still beneath the moulds. The passage to the hoist remains clear. Its death has not repaired the exposed counterweight below.
The Mortuary Custodian waits on the dais, articulated bronze and stone. Its mandating inscription is visible. Address it, present the specified authority, withdraw or risk a confrontation.
Inside the oilcloth chest lies a surveyor’s line and pitons. Choose a companion to carry it, then equip it for climbing and bracing.
A heavy bronze bearing lies beside the drum, stamped with the salvage company’s chalk. Edda’s commission pays six coins for this actual object.
The waxed refuge register lies on a stone reading stand. Its pages identify the families whose remains lie below.
A warded names lantern stands in the lampstand. It needs no oil in this bounded funerary enchantment; equipping it reveals the concealed funerary inscriptions.
A preserved relic rests in the offering tray. Inspect its actual equipment description before choosing a bearer; its fitted attachment changes that companion’s effective capabilities while equipped.
